claims.text: ASP.NET Core middleware registered with app.Use... calls runs in the exact order those calls appear in Program.cs.
A middleware can run code both before it calls the next delegate and after that call returns.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Middleware: write custom middleware

claims.text: A middleware short-circuits the pipeline by writing a response and not calling the next delegate; nothing registered after it then runs for that request.

ASP.NET Core's authorization middleware (app.UseAuthorization()), for an endpoint marked [Authorize], writes a 401 or 403 response itself and does not call the next delegate when the request is not permitted.
In DonHang.Api/Program.cs, the wiring calls run in this order: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, RequestLoggingMiddleware, UseCors, UseAuthentication, UseAuthorization, MapControllers.
RequestLoggingMiddleware starts a stopwatch, calls next(context), then logs the method, path, response status code, and elapsed time after next returns.

Sending POST /api/v1/orders to the running stage-1 lab with no Authorization header returns 401, and docker compose logs api shows a RequestLoggingMiddleware line for that request reporting status 401.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang stage-1 lab: docker compose logs api after curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders

self_check.notes: Outline item 3 named app.MapGet '(or similar)'; used app.MapControllers() as the 'or similar' case, consistent with the prior lesson. Short-circuit is illustrated via the real UseAuthorization()/[Authorize] behavior already in DonHang.Api (verified manually earlier: POST without a token returns 401) rather than new custom code, since no existing middleware in the repo demonstrates short-circuiting directly.
